_source: Extracted Nov 1 2026 from the Figma grape and style pages (scripts/extract-regions.mjs). Written from memory Oct 27 (Jeffrey to check).

grapes.name: CABERNET
grapes.description: Cabernet Sauvignon, the world’s most famous red grape. Thick skins give it deep color, firm tannin and dark fruit.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN RED WINE

taste.line: Big and bold. Built to age and to stand up to rich meat.

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: Bold tannin meets rich, braised beef.

pairs.name: Short Rib Arancini
pairs.why: A smaller bite, the same match.

grapes.sayIt: “A Cabernet. Full-bodied, with dark fruit and a firm finish.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Cabernet Sauvignon is a natural cross of Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc.

grapes.name: MERLOT
grapes.description: A softer, rounder red than Cabernet, with plum and chocolate. Easy to like.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN RED WINE

taste.line: Smooth and plush. A safe pick for most red drinkers.

pairs.name: Mike’s Vegas Pie
pairs.why: Plush enough for cheese and sauce.

grapes.sayIt: “A Merlot. Soft and smooth, with plum and a little chocolate.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Merlot is the most planted grape in Bordeaux.

grapes.name: PINOT NOIR
grapes.description: A light, silky red with red fruit and earth. Thin skins make it delicate and hard to grow.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN RED WINE

taste.line: Elegant and food-friendly. Great for guests who want a lighter red.

pairs.name: Agnolotti
pairs.why: Earthy and light enough for squash.

grapes.sayIt: “A Pinot Noir. Light and silky, with cherry and a little earth.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Pinot Noir’s thin skins make it hard to grow, which is why good bottles cost more.

grapes.name: SANGIOVESE
grapes.description: Italy’s most planted red grape. Tart cherry, tomato leaf and herbs, with bright acid.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN RED WINE

taste.line: Bright and savory. Made for tomato sauce and pizza.

pairs.name: Short Rib Arancini
pairs.why: Savory and fried, with cherry fruit.

grapes.sayIt: “A Sangiovese, the grape of Chianti. Cherry, herbs and bright acid.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Sangiovese is the main grape in Chianti and Brunello di Montalcino.

grapes.name: NEBBIOLO
grapes.description: The grape of Barolo and Barbaresco. Pale in color but powerful, with roses, tar and strong tannin.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN RED WINE

taste.line: Looks light, drinks big. Best with rich food.

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: Big tannin for a big braise.

pairs.name: Agnolotti
pairs.why: A classic Piedmont pairing with pasta.

grapes.sayIt: “A Nebbiolo, from Barolo country. Roses and cherry, with a strong finish.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Nebbiolo is named after nebbia, the fog that covers Piedmont’s hills at harvest.

grapes.name: SYRAH
grapes.description: A dark, full red with blackberry, black pepper and smoky, meaty notes.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN RED WINE

taste.line: Savory and spicy. Loves grilled and braised meat.

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: Peppery and meaty, like the braise.

pairs.name: Mike’s Vegas Pie
pairs.why: Bold enough for a hearty pie.

grapes.sayIt: “A Syrah. Dark fruit with black pepper and a little smoke.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Syrah and Shiraz are the same grape. Australia calls it Shiraz.

grapes.name: ZINFANDEL
grapes.description: California’s heritage grape. Ripe and jammy, with spice and often higher alcohol.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN RED WINE

taste.line: Bold, fruity and a little sweet-seeming.

pairs.name: Mike’s Vegas Pie
pairs.why: Jammy fruit with a hearty pie.

grapes.sayIt: “A Zinfandel. Big, ripe and jammy, with spice.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Zinfandel is genetically the same grape as Italy’s Primitivo.

grapes.name: MALBEC
grapes.description: A dark, plush red with blackberry, plum and cocoa. Argentina’s signature grape.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN RED WINE

taste.line: Smooth and full. Great value for a big red.

pairs.name: Short Rib Arancini
pairs.why: Dark fruit with a savory bite.

grapes.sayIt: “A Malbec. Dark, plush and smooth.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Malbec came from southwest France, but Argentina made it famous.

grapes.name: CHARDONNAY
grapes.description: The world’s most popular white grape. Crisp and appley without oak, or rich, buttery and toasty with oak.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WHITE WINE

taste.line: Ask: crisp, or rich and buttery? Chardonnay can be either.

pairs.name: Scallop Rockefeller
pairs.why: Rich wine with a rich, buttery topping.

pairs.name: Agnolotti
pairs.why: Round enough for squash and sweet potato.

grapes.sayIt: “A Chardonnay. This one is [crisp / rich and buttery].”
grapes.goodToKnow: Chablis is 100% Chardonnay, usually made with little or no oak.

grapes.name: SAUVIGNON BLANC
grapes.description: A zesty, refreshing white with citrus, green apple and fresh-cut grass.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WHITE WINE

taste.line: Bright and tangy. A great first glass.

pairs.name: Beet Confit
pairs.why: Tangy wine with crème fraîche and orange.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: Zesty acid cuts the crispy crust.

grapes.sayIt: “A Sauvignon Blanc. Zesty and bright, with grapefruit and lime.”
grapes.goodToKnow: White Sancerre, from France’s Loire Valley, is 100% Sauvignon Blanc.

grapes.name: PINOT GRIGIO
grapes.description: A light, clean white with pear, lemon and a mineral finish. Easy to drink.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WHITE WINE

taste.line: Light and crisp. Goes with almost anything.

grapes.sayIt: “A Pinot Grigio. Light and crisp, with pear and lemon.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Pinot Grigio and Pinot Gris are the same grape. Gris means gray, for its pinkish skin.

grapes.name: RIESLING
grapes.description: An aromatic white with lime, peach and a mineral edge. It can be bone dry or sweet, always with bright acid.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WHITE WINE

taste.line: Bright and aromatic. Great with spice.

pairs.name: Cauliflower
pairs.why: Bright acid lifts the roasted flavor.

grapes.sayIt: “A Riesling. This one is [dry / off-dry], with lime and peach.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Northern Michigan is known for Riesling. Ask the guest if they want dry or sweet.

grapes.name: PECORINO
grapes.description: An Italian white grape from the Marche and Abruzzo. Crisp and herbal, with citrus and a little salinity.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WHITE WINE

taste.line: Crisp and savory.

pairs.name: Mini Lemon Ricotta Ravioli
pairs.why: Citrus and herbs with lemon and ricotta.

grapes.sayIt: “A Pecorino from Italy. Crisp and a little herbal. It’s lovely with the walleye.”
grapes.goodToKnow: The grape shares its name with the cheese. It nearly disappeared before growers revived it in the 1980s.

grapes.name: CHENIN BLANC
grapes.description: A versatile white with apple, quince and honey. Made dry, sweet or sparkling.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WHITE WINE

taste.line: Rich but bright. Sweet versions are great with dessert.

pairs.name: Scallop Rockefeller
pairs.why: Bright acid with a rich topping.

grapes.sayIt: “A Chenin Blanc. Apple and honey, with bright acid.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Vouvray, in France’s Loire Valley, is made from Chenin Blanc.

grapes.name: PROVENCE
grapes.description: The classic pale pink rosé from the south of France. Usually a blend of Grenache, Cinsault and Syrah.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN ROSÉ WINE

taste.line: Dry, crisp and delicate. The style most guests picture.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: Light and crisp with fried fish.

grapes.sayIt: “A Provence rosé. Pale, dry and crisp.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Most of the wine made in Provence is rosé.

grapes.name: ROSATO
grapes.description: Rosato is Italian for rosé. Often a little deeper in color and fruitier than Provence.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN ROSÉ WINE

taste.line: Fruity, dry and food-friendly.

pairs.name: Mike’s Vegas Pie
pairs.why: Enough fruit for cheese and sauce.

grapes.sayIt: “An Italian rosato. Dry, with cherry and watermelon.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Many Italian rosatos come from the south, like Puglia and Sicily.

grapes.name: PINOT NOIR ROSÉ
grapes.description: Rosé made from Pinot Noir. Delicate, with red berries and bright acid.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN ROSÉ WINE

taste.line: Light and refreshing. Great as a first glass.

pairs.name: Cauliflower
pairs.why: Light enough to let it shine.

pairs.name: Scallop Rockefeller
pairs.why: Bright acid with a rich topping.

grapes.sayIt: “A rosé of Pinot Noir. Pale and bright, with raspberry.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Rosé of Pinot Noir is usually very pale, because Pinot has thin skins.

grapes.name: SPARKLING ROSÉ
grapes.description: Pink sparkling wine, from rosé Champagne to Prosecco Rosé. Red berries and bubbles.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN ROSÉ WINE

taste.line: Festive and food-friendly. Great for celebrations.

grapes.sayIt: “A sparkling rosé. Red berries and bubbles. Great for a celebration.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Most rosé Champagne is made by blending a little red wine into white before the bubbles.

grapes.name: QVEVRI
grapes.script: White wine made like a red
grapes.description: Georgia’s ancient method: white grapes fermented and aged with their skins in clay jars called qvevri, buried in the ground.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN ORANGE WINE

taste.line: Bold and textured. The original orange wine.

pairs.name: Cauliflower
pairs.why: Nutty wine for roasted, nutty food.

grapes.sayIt: “An orange wine from Georgia, made in clay. Dry, nutty and bold.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Georgia has made wine in qvevri for about 8,000 years. UNESCO lists the method as cultural heritage.

grapes.name: RIBOLLA GIALLA
grapes.script: White wine made like a red
grapes.description: A white grape from Friuli that’s often made with long skin contact. Savory, with stone fruit and a gentle grip.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN ORANGE WINE

taste.line: Savory and structured. A favorite of orange wine fans.

grapes.sayIt: “A Ribolla Gialla, an orange wine from northeast Italy. Savory and textured.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Ribolla Gialla grows on both sides of the Italy–Slovenia border.

grapes.name: RAMATO
grapes.script: White wine made like a red
grapes.description: Pinot Grigio left on its pinkish skins for a short time, giving a copper color. Lighter than most orange wines.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN ORANGE WINE

taste.line: An easy first step into orange wine.

grapes.sayIt: “A ramato, a copper Pinot Grigio. Light, with pear and a little spice.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Ramato means “copper” in Italian.

grapes.name: AMERICAN ORANGE
grapes.script: White wine made like a red
grapes.description: American winemakers making skin-contact whites, often from aromatic grapes. Fresh, fruity and a little funky.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN ORANGE WINE

taste.line: Brighter and fruitier than the Old World styles.

grapes.sayIt: “An American orange wine. Fresh, fruity and a little funky.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Many American orange wines are also natural wines, made with very little intervention.

grapes.name: CHAMPAGNE
grapes.description: Sparkling wine from the Champagne region of France, with bubbles made in the bottle. Toasty, fine and elegant.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SPARKLING WINE

taste.line: The benchmark. Fine bubbles and toasty, bready notes.

grapes.sayIt: “A Champagne. Fine bubbles, with toast and green apple.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Non-vintage Champagne must age at least 15 months before release. Vintage needs 3 years.

grapes.name: PROSECCO
grapes.description: Italy’s popular sparkling wine, from the Glera grape in the Veneto. Light, fruity and easy.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SPARKLING WINE

taste.line: Fresh and fun. The base of the Aperol Spritz.

pairs.name: Short Rib Arancini
pairs.why: Light bubbles with a fried bite.

grapes.sayIt: “A Prosecco. Light and fruity, with pear and green apple.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Prosecco gets its bubbles in a large tank, which keeps it fresh and fruity.

grapes.name: CAVA
grapes.description: Spain’s sparkling wine, made the same way as Champagne. Dry, crisp and great value.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SPARKLING WINE

taste.line: Champagne-style bubbles at a friendlier price.

grapes.sayIt: “A Cava from Spain. Dry and crisp, made like Champagne.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Cava is made the same way as Champagne, with bubbles made in the bottle.

grapes.name: CRÉMANT
grapes.description: French sparkling wine made the Champagne way, but in other regions like the Loire, Burgundy and Alsace.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SPARKLING WINE

taste.line: Champagne quality without the Champagne price.

grapes.sayIt: “A Crémant. French bubbles made like Champagne, from another region.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Crémant is French sparkling wine made the Champagne way, outside Champagne.

grapes.name: FRANCIACORTA
grapes.description: Italy’s answer to Champagne, from Lombardy. Bottle-fermented, rich and creamy.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SPARKLING WINE

taste.line: Rich and elegant. A step up from Prosecco.

grapes.sayIt: “A Franciacorta. Italian, made like Champagne. Creamy and elegant.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Franciacorta is made the Champagne way, in Lombardy, northern Italy.

grapes.name: AMERICAN
grapes.description: American sparkling wine, often made the Champagne way with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Riper and fruitier.
grapes.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SPARKLING WINE

taste.line: Champagne style with sunny California fruit.

grapes.sayIt: “An American sparkling wine. Made like Champagne, with riper fruit.”
grapes.goodToKnow: Several Champagne houses own California wineries, like Roederer Estate and Domaine Carneros.
